title: POC scoping: hosted vs dedicated vs private - Apex Analytics
summary: Initial POC scoping to decide between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Discussed success criteria (latency SLOs, cost targets, data residency), workload sizing (concurrent QPS, tokens per request, daily tokens), benchmark plan, timelines for a 4-week pilot, and next steps: benchmark run, security docs, pricing for dedicated tier.
topics: Deployment decision criteria (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
action_items: Devon - run baseline benchmarks using Apex sample prompts & dataset and share spreadsheet - due 2026-03-11
Maria - send dedicated pricing sheet and contract template - due 2026-03-06
Sam - provide sample prompts, schema, and network constraints (VPC peering/firewall) - due 2026-03-05
Lina - provide evaluation rubric and quality thresholds (F1/accuracy/QA pass rates) - due 2026-03-06
next_steps: Redwood to run 1-week benchmark across 2 model variants (quantized & fp16) using Apex payloads
Share SOC2/ISO and network architecture docs
Deliver preliminary cost estimate for Hosted vs Dedicated by 2026-03-06
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 16:00 UTC | duration 48m | recorded by Fireflies
Attendees: Maria Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Patel (Redwood SE), Ravi Kapoor (CTO, Apex), Lina Torres (Head of ML, Apex), Sam Nguyen (Infra Lead, Apex)

[00:00:03] Maria Chen (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros? we got about 45 minutes, want to focus on POC goals and pick the right deployment mode — hosted, dedicated, or private.
[00:00:12] Ravi Kapoor (Apex): Yep thanks Maria. I'll kick off. I'm Ravi, CTO. Lina runs the models day-to-day, Sam runs infra. Our big ask: we want a semantic search + assistant product for customer support and internal analytics, and we need to decide where to run it.
[00:00:25] Lina Torres (Apex): hi all. Our current stack: embeddings on our vector DB (Pinecone), some in-house reranker, and a small chat assistant running on hosted model APIs. Latency and cost are becoming an issue at scale.
[00:00:38] Maria Chen (Redwood): Understood. quick question on workload sizing — what are peak concurrent requests, avg tokens per request, and daily volume?
[00:00:46] Lina Torres (Apex): Roughly peak concurrent requests ~120 at busy times, avg payload ~110 tokens per request, peaks up to 250 tokens for some analytics prompts. Daily tokens maybe 3.5 to 5 million tokens.
[00:01:02] Sam Nguyen (Apex): And we prioritize 95th pct latency under 700ms for interactive flows, cost target is roughly $X per 1M tokens — we can give exact later. Also data residency: some customer transcripts must remain in EU and be encrypted with our KMS.
[00:01:18] Devon Patel (Redwood SE): ok good data. so the decision axis is clear: latency/cost, data residency & compliance, and ops overhead. quick topo: Hosted is fastest to stand up, low ops, good for non-sensitive data and dev evals; Dedicated gives predictable throughput, reserved GPU pools, better tail latency and cost predictability; Private (VPC/on-prem) is for strict residency and air-gapped needs with our private control plane.
[00:01:43] Ravi Kapoor (Apex): A couple of clarifying q's: for Dedicated, do we get VPC peering? and is there a KMS integration?
[00:01:50] Maria Chen (Redwood): yes Dedicated supports VPC peering and customer-managed KMS (Cloud KMS or HSM integrations). Private gives full control with on-prem options and can run in your VPC with no customer data leaving the environment.
[00:02:03] Lina Torres (Apex): for Hosted, what's the 95th pct latency realistically for our payload sizes? we saw some vendors at 95th ~1.2s which is too slow for interactive chat.
[00:02:11] Devon Patel (Redwood SE): For hosted, depends on model and seq length and burst patterns. For a 120-token req on our curated open models we'd expect 95th in the 400-800ms range if sequence caching and batching are favorable; if you need stricter 95th <500ms then Dedicated with pinned capacity or model quantization profiles is safer.
[00:02:29] Sam Nguyen (Apex): how do we validate quality? we'd like a pass-fail on our eval set not just latency.
[00:02:35] Devon Patel (Redwood SE): we'll run your eval prompts, compute quality metrics you define (e.g., retrieval accuracy, F1, human-A/B), and measure token cost and latency simultaneously. we do a benchmark sweep: fp16 and int8 quantized variants, plus an endpoint with prefix/KV cache on to simulate chat reuse.
[00:02:51] Maria Chen (Redwood): timeline thoughts — if we agree, Redwood can run a 1-week benchmark, then a 4-week pilot. the bench will give latency/cost numbers so you can decide whether Hosted is sufficient or you need Dedicated or Private.
[00:03:03] Ravi Kapoor (Apex): sounds good. what's included in the benchmark deliverable?
[00:03:07] Devon Patel (Redwood SE): spreadsheet with per-model lines: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec throughput, cost per 1M tokens, memory/kv usage, and sample outputs for QA. plus notes on kernel/quantization choices. we'll also include recommendations: e.g., for your workload Model-A quantized on Dedicated hits 95th 420ms at 120 conc while Hosted Model-A at burst drops to 700ms.
[00:03:28] Lina Torres (Apex): okay realistic constraints: we need SOC2, SAML SSO for user access, audit logs, and for some customers EU-only storage. any blockers there?
[00:03:36] Maria Chen (Redwood): Redwood has SOC2 and ISO docs we can share. SAML/SSO and RBAC are supported in Dedicated and Private; Hosted also supports enterprise SSO for managed accounts. EU-only data residency is easiest with Private or Dedicated in EU region; Hosted can be region-pinned but there are data flow considerations we'll document.
[00:03:53] Sam Nguyen (Apex): network constraints: we cannot allow egress through nat for certain data sets. can Dedicated or Private support private networking?
[00:03:59] Devon Patel (Redwood SE): yes Dedicated supports VPC peering and controlled egress; Private can be fully air-gapped. We'll capture the exact firewall rules we need in the network runbook.
[00:04:09] Ravi Kapoor (Apex): cost question — for Dedicated, is there a commit, and how does autoscaling work?
[00:04:13] Maria Chen (Redwood): Dedicated is a reserved capacity contract (monthly/annual). It supports configurable autoscaling and burst capacity; pricing depends on committed GPU pool and agreed throughput. we'll send a sample pricing sheet.
[00:04:24] Lina Torres (Apex): great. for success criteria: 95th pct latency <500ms for chat, quality parity (>= current baseline) on 5 eval tasks, and cost under target X (we'll share). if we hit those in the pilot, we'll expand to prod.
[00:04:38] Devon Patel (Redwood SE): noted. we'll design the benchmark to measure those three axes. one detail: for chat flows prefix caching can dramatically reduce tokens and latencies; we'll simulate real session reuse.
[00:04:50] Ravi Kapoor (Apex): what's the sample size for benchmark? how many prompts/requests?
[00:04:54] Devon Patel (Redwood SE): recommend 10k varied prompts covering short and long seqs; run under a concurrency profile that matches your 24-hour peaks and burst patterns. we'll coordinate on the exact dataset.
[00:05:06] Sam Nguyen (Apex): timeline — if bench results look good, we want to start a 4-week pilot targeting a small subset of traffic by late March. is that feasible?
[00:05:12] Maria Chen (Redwood): yep feasible. proposed timeline: share sample prompts + rubric by 3/5, Redwood runs bench 3/6-3/11, deliver results 3/12, pilot kickoff 3/16 with a 4-week window.
[00:05:25] Lina Torres (Apex): ok that works. some compliance folks will want a security review — we'll loop them in after we get docs.
[00:05:31] Maria Chen (Redwood): we'll include SOC2, ISO, network runbook, and KMS integration notes in the folder we share.
[00:05:36] Ravi Kapoor (Apex): any red flags we should be aware of?
[00:05:39] Devon Patel (Redwood SE): only potential ones: if your bursts spike well beyond the reserved capacity we plan for, Hosted may throttle or latency will rise; Dedicated needs the right commit to hit your 95th target. Private has more setup time but addresses all residency/egress needs. Also model quality regressions when quantizing — we'll surface those in the bench.
[00:05:57] Sam Nguyen (Apex): ok let's talk concrete next steps.
[00:05:59] Maria Chen (Redwood): action items recap: Devon will run bench with Apex data, Maria will send pricing and legal basics, Sam will share prompts and network constraints, Lina will share eval rubric. I'll also schedule the technical kickoff.
[00:06:12] Ravi Kapoor (Apex): agreed. can you include a cost compare: Hosted vs Dedicated committed vs Dedicated burst?
[00:06:16] Maria Chen (Redwood): yes we'll include per-1M token cost and an example monthly commit scenario.
[00:06:21] Lina Torres (Apex): final question — for the pilot do you need service accounts/keys from us?
[00:06:25] Devon Patel (Redwood SE): we'll need a service account and sample payloads; for private or dedicated we may need VPC peering details. we'll send a checklist.
[00:06:33] Maria Chen (Redwood): thanks everyone. we'll share the benchmark plan and a calendar invite for 3/9 tech kickoff.
[00:06:38] Ravi Kapoor (Apex): thanks.
[00:06:39] Meeting end

Notes: transcript has minor transcription artifacts; speaker turns sometimes overlapped. references: "kv cache" sometimes transcribed as "k-v cash", product names may be misheard. Shared artifacts: Redwood benchmark template spreadsheet (link sent after call), SOC2+ISO pack (link), dedicated-pricing-sheet.pdf (link).
